resources.string: Offline Wi-Fi hotspot and USB/Ethernet LAN setup
Device testing is still needed. Use a game with LAN or direct-IP multiplayer. LAN setup does not add multiplayer to a game or replace Steam authentication. Set this up before launching the game.

Host creates a password-protected local network without a router or internet. It may disconnect your current Wi-Fi. On the other device, join using Android Wi-Fi settings and choose to stay connected without internet. Then select the LAN interface below on both devices. If cellular takes priority, turn mobile data off while playing.
Offline hotspot requested. Tap to manage LAN.
Android could not start a usable hotspot on this device.
Turn off any existing hotspot or Wi-Fi Direct connection, then try again.
Hotspots are disabled by this device’s policy.
No Wi-Fi channel is available. Check Wi-Fi and airplane mode, then retry.
Hosting needs precise location permission for this app’s Android compatibility level. Enable it in App settings, then retry.
Turn on Android Location services, then retry hosting.

Connect a data-capable USB-C cable and enable USB tethering on one device in Android settings. This only works if the other device supports the USB network driver and host role. If no LAN interface appears, try reversing the cable’s host/device roles or use USB Ethernet adapters. Charging or file-transfer mode alone does not create a LAN. DroidDeck cannot enable USB tethering itself.

Select the interface whose IP belongs to your local connection. DroidDeck reports this interface and its real index to the Linux session. This does not change Android routing; use the host’s IP in the game if LAN discovery fails. Selection lasts until the app process exits or you return to the default below.
No local IPv4 interfaces are visible yet. Connect the devices first.
%1$s is unavailable. Reconnect or choose another interface.
